title: Vacation Supply Days — Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit Calculation Standard
content:
**Calculation.** Under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, the vacation supply for the drug of the member's most recent paid network claim is a number of whole days, defined as follows.

1. The vacation ceiling is the network's maximum days supply of a vacation override.
2. The supply on hand for the vacation is the days not yet run out, as of today and counting the fill's date of service as day zero, of the member's most recent paid network claim for the drug, or zero with no such claim. The days not yet run out are that claim's days supply less the calendar days from its date of service to today, never below zero.
3. The vacation supply is the vacation ceiling less the supply on hand for the vacation, never below zero, in whole days.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs, vacation ceiling taken as 60 days)

| Most recent paid network claim for the drug | Today | Supply on hand | Vacation supply |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days, dated day 0 | Day 20 | 10 | 60 less 10, that is 50 |
| 30 days, dated day 0 | Day 30 | 0 | 60 |
| 90 days, dated day 0 | Day 10 | 80 | 0 (never below zero) |
| None | — | 0 | 60 |

## Reading the definition

- The drug is fixed by the member's most recent paid network claim, whichever drug that is.
- The supply on hand is counted as of today, the day the vacation supply is worked out; the departure date does not enter the figure.
